functions.name: jerry_debugger_transport_add
functions.signature:
void jerry_debugger_transport_add (jerry_debugger_transport_header_t *header_p,
                                   size_t send_message_header_size,
                                   size_t max_send_message_size,
                                   size_t receive_message_header_size,
                                   size_t max_receive_message_size);
functions.description: Registers a transport interface with the JerryScript debugger transport layer, supplying per-transport header sizes and maximum payload sizes for send/receive paths. The function links the transport into the internal list and initializes fields the framework owns.
requirements: header_p must be a valid, initialized pointer
Before calling, header_p->close, header_p->send, and header_p->receive must be set (explicitly stated in comments)
header_p->next_p is managed/finalized by this function (caller must not rely on or pre-set it)
Size parameters are size_t; specific bounds are not documented here (unknown).

functions.name: jerry_debugger_transport_start
functions.description: Starts the debugger transport subsystem, enabling connection establishment and I/O via previously added transports. Typical usage is to call this after one or more transports have been added.
requirements: Should be called after at least one jerry_debugger_transport_add (inferred from naming and typical init flow; exact requirement not documented—unknown)

functions.name: jerry_debugger_transport_is_connected
functions.description: Returns whether the debugger transport layer currently has an active connection. Useful to gate send/receive operations or drive connection-dependent logic.
requirements: None beyond standard call semantics; no parameters. The precise meaning of "connected" is not further documented here (unknown).

functions.name: jerry_debugger_transport_close
functions.description: Closes the active debugger transport connection(s). Implementations are expected to invoke the registered transport close callback(s) and release associated resources.
requirements: Should only be called when the transport subsystem has been started or a transport has been added (inferred; exact preconditions not documented—unknown)
After close, further send/receive calls may fail or be ignored (inferred—unknown).

functions.name: jerry_debugger_transport_send
functions.description: Sends a binary message through the debugger transport layer. Returns true on successful transmission, false otherwise. Intended for framing/debugger protocol messages prepared by the caller.
requirements: message_p must be a valid pointer to at least message_length bytes (if message_length > 0).
Should be called only when jerry_debugger_transport_is_connected() is true (inferred; not explicitly stated—unknown).
message_length is expected to be within the configured max_send_message_size given at jerry_debugger_transport_add (inferred—unknown).

functions.name: jerry_debugger_transport_receive
functions.description: Attempts to receive data from the debugger transport into the provided receive context. The context tracks the buffer, accumulated bytes, and message framing. Returns true if data was received/advanced, false otherwise. For datagram protocols, message_total_length holds the full datagram length; for stream protocols it remains 0.
requirements: context_p must be a valid, non-null pointer.
context_p->buffer_p must point to writable storage large enough for incoming data (size not specified here—unknown).
The fields received_length, message_p, message_length, and message_total_length must be initialized according to the caller’s receive strategy or previous calls (not fully documented—unknown).

functions.name: jerry_debugger_transport_receive_completed
functions.description: Signals that processing of the current received message in context_p is complete, allowing the transport layer to finalize or advance the receive state for the next message.
requirements: context_p must be the same context previously used with jerry_debugger_transport_receive.
context_p must be valid and consistent with the transport’s expectations (exact state requirements are not documented—unknown).

functions.name: jerry_debugger_transport_sleep
functions.description: Puts the debugger transport handling into a brief sleep/yield state. Typically used to avoid busy-waiting when polling transports.
requirements: No parameters; timing and duration are unspecified (unknown).

functions.name: jerry_debugger_is_connected
functions.description: Returns whether a debugger client is currently connected to the JerryScript engine. Typical usage: check before attempting debugger-only operations such as sending output or waiting for client-provided sources.
requirements: May be called at any time to query connection state.
No arguments; no side effects are implied by the signature.
Return value is a boolean indicating connection state; callers should branch accordingly.

functions.name: jerry_debugger_stop
functions.description: Requests the engine to enter a stopped/break state for the debugger (i.e., trigger a pause). Intended for use when a debugger client is connected to break execution programmatically.
requirements: Should be called only when debugger support is enabled in the engine; otherwise behavior is implementation-defined/unknown.
Intended to be used when a debugger client is connected (use jerry_debugger_is_connected to check); exact behavior if no client is connected is unknown.

functions.name: jerry_debugger_continue
functions.description: Requests the engine to resume execution if it is currently paused/stopped by the debugger.
requirements: Meaningful only if execution is currently paused by the debugger; otherwise has no effect or effect is implementation-defined/unknown.
Should be used in conjunction with debugger pause/step behavior; exact error/return handling is unknown since the function returns void.

functions.name: jerry_debugger_stop_at_breakpoint
functions.description: Enables or disables stopping at breakpoints. When enabled, the engine will stop at breakpoints; when disabled, it will not break on them.
requirements: Parameter enable_stop_at_breakpoint is a boolean flag; pass true to enable, false to disable.
Can be called regardless of connection state, but effect when no debugger client is connected is unknown.
No return value; callers should not assume synchronous pausing occurs immediately upon calling—behavior is controlled by engine breakpoint handling.

functions.name: jerry_debugger_wait_for_client_source
functions.description: Waits for source code sent by a connected debugger client and processes it via the provided callback. Returns a status indicating whether a source was received, reception failed, end-of-sources was signaled, or a context reset was requested. The callback receives the source name, source code, and the user pointer, and returns a jerry_value_t which is passed back to the caller via return_value (naming suggests parity with a related API; exact return semantics for this function are partially undocumented in this header).
requirements: A valid function pointer callback_p that matches jerry_debugger_wait_for_source_callback_t must be provided; whether NULL is allowed is unknown.
user_p is an opaque pointer passed through to the callback; no specific requirements beyond being safely dereferenceable by the callback’s logic (if it dereferences it).
return_value must point to writable storage for a jerry_value_t if the caller expects the callback’s return to be captured; whether NULL is allowed (to ignore the value) is unknown.

Caller should be prepared to handle all jerry_debugger_wait_for_source_status_t outcomes: JERRY_DEBUGGER_SOURCE_RECEIVE_FAILED, JERRY_DEBUGGER_SOURCE_RECEIVED, JERRY_DEBUGGER_SOURCE_END, JERRY_DEBUGGER_CONTEXT_RESET_RECEIVED.
Must be called when a debugger client connection is expected/available; behavior when no client is connected is unknown.
The callback must not assume NUL-termination of source_name_p or source_p; sizes are provided (source_name_size, source_size).
The callback must treat source_name_p and source_p as read-only for the duration of the call.

functions.name: jerry_debugger_send_output
functions.description: Sends the given text buffer to the connected debugger client’s output channel (e.g., console/log). Intended for transmitting runtime output over the debugger transport.
requirements: buffer must point to at least str_size bytes of readable memory; it need not be NUL-terminated.
str_size specifies the number of bytes/characters to send and should accurately reflect the buffer length to avoid truncation or reading past the end.
Behavior when no debugger client is connected is unknown; callers should consider checking jerry_debugger_is_connected.
Thread-safety and reentrancy are unspecified; avoid calling concurrently unless the embedding guarantees safety.

functions.name: jerry_generate_snapshot
functions.signature:
jerry_value_t jerry_generate_snapshot (jerry_value_t compiled_code,
                                       uint32_t generate_snapshot_opts,
                                       uint32_t *buffer_p,
                                       size_t buffer_size);
functions.description: Generate a JerryScript snapshot from an already compiled script or function value. Callers provide a writable buffer to receive the snapshot and may control generation with the provided bitmask flags (e.g., static snapshot). Returns a JerryScript value indicating the result (implementation-defined).
requirements: compiled_code must be a valid compiled/parsed JerryScript code or function value suitable for snapshotting (inferred from parameter name and API).
generate_snapshot_opts must be a bitmask composed of jerry_generate_snapshot_opts_t flags (e.g., JERRY_SNAPSHOT_SAVE_STATIC).
buffer_p must point to writable memory sufficient to hold the produced snapshot; buffer_size must specify its size (unit as required by the API; inferred from pointer type).
buffer_p must be suitably aligned for uint32_t writes (inferred from parameter type).
The function must be called in a properly initialized JerryScript engine context (inferred from API usage).

functions.name: jerry_exec_snapshot
functions.signature:
jerry_value_t jerry_exec_snapshot (const uint32_t *snapshot_p,
                                   size_t snapshot_size,
                                   size_t func_index,
                                   uint32_t exec_snapshot_opts,
                                   const jerry_exec_snapshot_option_values_t *options_values_p);
functions.description: Execute a JerryScript snapshot or load a function from it, depending on flags. The snapshot buffer and its size are provided by the caller. Optional execution options control behavior such as copying data, allowing static snapshots, loading as a function, and setting source name or user value for created functions. Returns a JerryScript value with the result of execution or the loaded function (implementation-defined).
requirements: snapshot_p must point to a valid snapshot previously generated by the JerryScript snapshot APIs (inferred from name and usage).
snapshot_size must correspond to the total size of the snapshot buffer (inferred from signature).
func_index selects the function to load when JERRY_SNAPSHOT_EXEC_LOAD_AS_FUNCTION is set (inferred from flag description).

exec_snapshot_opts must be a bitmask composed of jerry_exec_snapshot_opts_t flags (JERRY_SNAPSHOT_EXEC_COPY_DATA, JERRY_SNAPSHOT_EXEC_ALLOW_STATIC, JERRY_SNAPSHOT_EXEC_LOAD_AS_FUNCTION, JERRY_SNAPSHOT_EXEC_HAS_SOURCE_NAME, JERRY_SNAPSHOT_EXEC_HAS_USER_VALUE).
If JERRY_SNAPSHOT_EXEC_HAS_SOURCE_NAME is set, options_values_p->source_name is considered; non-string values are ignored (explicit).
If JERRY_SNAPSHOT_EXEC_HAS_USER_VALUE is set, options_values_p->user_value is assigned to all functions created by the script, including eval calls (explicit).
options_values_p may be NULL if no optional values are provided (inferred from being a pointer and flags gating usage).
snapshot_p must be suitably aligned for uint32_t reads (inferred from parameter type).
The function must be called in a properly initialized JerryScript engine context (inferred from API usage).

functions.name: jerry_merge_snapshots
functions.signature:
size_t jerry_merge_snapshots (const uint32_t **inp_buffers_p,
                              size_t *inp_buffer_sizes_p,
                              size_t number_of_snapshots,
                              uint32_t *out_buffer_p,
                              size_t out_buffer_size,
                              const char **error_p);
functions.description: Merge multiple JerryScript snapshots into a single snapshot. Callers pass arrays of input snapshot pointers and their sizes, plus a writable output buffer. On error, an error message may be provided via error_p. Returns the size of the merged snapshot (implementation-defined) or a value indicating failure (implementation-defined).
requirements: inp_buffers_p must point to an array of number_of_snapshots pointers to valid snapshot data (inferred from names and types).
inp_buffer_sizes_p must point to an array of number_of_snapshots sizes corresponding to each input snapshot (inferred).
number_of_snapshots must equal the number of elements in inp_buffers_p and inp_buffer_sizes_p (inferred).
out_buffer_p must point to writable memory of at least out_buffer_size (inferred).
All snapshot buffers must be suitably aligned for uint32_t access (inferred from parameter types).
error_p, if non-NULL, may receive a pointer to a human-readable error message on failure (inferred from type and name).
The function must be called in a properly initialized JerryScript engine context (inferred from API usage).

functions.name: jerry_get_literals_from_snapshot
functions.signature:
size_t jerry_get_literals_from_snapshot (const uint32_t *snapshot_p,
                                         size_t snapshot_size,
                                         jerry_char_t *lit_buf_p,
                                         size_t lit_buf_size,
                                         bool is_c_format);
functions.description: Extract literal strings embedded in a JerryScript snapshot into a caller-provided character buffer. The output can be formatted as C source compatible text when requested. Returns the amount of data written or required (implementation-defined).
requirements: snapshot_p must point to a valid snapshot buffer; snapshot_size must describe its size (inferred).
lit_buf_p must point to a writable buffer of at least lit_buf_size elements of jerry_char_t (explicit from types and names).
is_c_format selects whether the literals are output in a C-friendly format (explicit from parameter name and comment).
snapshot_p must be suitably aligned for uint32_t reads (inferred from parameter type).
The function must be called in a properly initialized JerryScript engine context (inferred from API usage).

functions.name: jerry_port_init
functions.description: Initializes the JerryScript port layer for the host program. Typically called early in program startup (before using the engine) to let the port set up any required resources.

No arguments; safe to call exactly once per process unless the specific port states otherwise (details unknown).

functions.name: jerry_port_fatal
functions.description: Terminates the process due to an unrecoverable failure. Intended to be called by the engine to abort execution; a libc-based port may implement using exit() or abort().
requirements: The code argument must be a valid jerry_fatal_code_t value (e.g., JERRY_FATAL_OUT_OF_MEMORY, JERRY_FATAL_REF_COUNT_LIMIT, etc.).

functions.name: jerry_port_sleep
functions.description: Sleeps the current process/thread for the specified number of milliseconds. Used by jerry-core only when JERRY_DEBUGGER is enabled.
requirements: sleep_time is a duration in milliseconds as an unsigned 32-bit value.
Only meaningful when the debugger support is enabled; otherwise typically unused.

functions.name: jerry_port_context_alloc
functions.description: Allocates external context storage for the engine when JERRY_EXTERNAL_CONTEXT is enabled. The engine passes the required internal context size; the port may allocate more to supply an internal heap. Returns the total size of the allocated buffer.
requirements: The returned memory must be pointer-aligned; otherwise behavior is undefined (requirement on implementation; caller should rely on this).
The allocated size must be at least context_size (implementation guarantee).
Only called/used when JERRY_EXTERNAL_CONTEXT is enabled; otherwise unused.

functions.name: jerry_port_context_get
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the currently active JerryScript engine context when JERRY_EXTERNAL_CONTEXT is enabled.
requirements: Must return the pointer to the currently used engine context (implementation guarantee).
Only called/used when JERRY_EXTERNAL_CONTEXT is enabled.

functions.name: jerry_port_context_free
functions.description: Frees the currently used engine context when JERRY_EXTERNAL_CONTEXT is enabled. Typically invoked by jerry_cleanup.
requirements: Should only be called after a context has been allocated/initialized (inferred from purpose).
Only called/used when JERRY_EXTERNAL_CONTEXT is enabled.

functions.name: jerry_port_log
functions.description: Logs or displays a debug/error message from the engine. Messages are zero-terminated and may arrive in parts across multiple calls; the implementation should handle partial messages appropriately.
requirements: message_p must point to a zero-terminated string.
Callers may pass multiple message parts; implementations should not assume messages are complete per call.

functions.name: jerry_port_print_buffer
functions.description: Prints a raw character buffer to standard output. Used by jerry-ext components to emit information.
requirements: buffer_p must point to at least buffer_size bytes of readable data.
This function is not called from jerry-core directly; used by extensions.

functions.name: jerry_port_line_read
functions.description: Reads a line from standard input. The returned string includes the line terminator(s) and is zero-terminated. Returns NULL to signal end-of-input or an error. The caller must later free a non-NULL result via jerry_port_line_free.
requirements: out_size_p receives the input string size in bytes, excluding the terminating zero byte.
If the return value is non-NULL, the caller must pass it to jerry_port_line_free when no longer needed.
Callers must tolerate NULL return indicating end-of-input or error.

functions.name: jerry_port_line_free
functions.description: Frees a line buffer previously allocated/returned by jerry_port_line_read.
requirements: buffer_p must be a pointer returned by jerry_port_line_read.
Should be called when the line buffer is no longer needed.

functions.name: jerry_port_path_normalize
functions.description: Canonicalizes a filesystem path. Implementations should resolve symbolic links and directory references where possible, returning a newly allocated, normalized path string. Returns NULL on error. The caller must free a non-NULL result using jerry_port_path_free.
requirements: path_p must point to a zero-terminated input path string; path_size is its size in bytes excluding the terminating zero.
The returned non-NULL buffer must be freed with jerry_port_path_free.
The implementation must not return the input buffer directly; callers should not assume identity between input and output.
On NULL return, the caller must not proceed with operations requiring a canonical path.

functions.name: jerry_port_path_free
functions.description: Frees a path buffer that was returned by jerry_port_path_normalize.
requirements: path_p must be a buffer previously returned by jerry_port_path_normalize.

functions.name: jerry_port_path_base
functions.description: Returns the offset (index) of the first character of the basename component within the given path, i.e., the character after the last path separator. Used to split path into directory and file name.
requirements: path_p must be a zero-terminated path string.

functions.name: jerry_port_source_read
functions.description: Opens a source file at file_name_p and reads its entire contents into a newly allocated buffer. The size in bytes is returned via out_size_p. The caller must free the buffer with jerry_port_source_free when done.
requirements: file_name_p must be a valid filesystem path to the source file.
out_size_p must be a valid pointer to receive the file size in bytes.
On non-NULL return, the caller must free the buffer with jerry_port_source_free when no longer needed.

functions.name: jerry_port_source_free
functions.description: Frees a source file buffer previously returned by jerry_port_source_read.
requirements: buffer_p must be a buffer returned by jerry_port_source_read.

functions.name: jerry_port_local_tza
functions.description: Returns the local time zone adjustment in milliseconds for a given time, specified as milliseconds since Unix epoch. Should match ECMAScript LocalTZA behavior (ES12, 21.4.1.7) as if called with isUTC = true.
requirements: unix_ms is a time value in milliseconds since Unix epoch.
Only used when JERRY_BUILTIN_DATE is enabled.

functions.name: jerry_port_current_time
functions.description: Returns the current system time in UTC as milliseconds since Unix epoch. Also usable to seed a random number generator.
requirements: Only called/used when JERRY_BUILTIN_DATE is enabled (by jerry-core), but can be used by applications as needed.

functions.name: jerryx_arg_transform_this_and_args
functions.signature: jerry_value_t jerryx_arg_transform_this_and_args (const jerry_value_t this_val, const jerry_value_t *js_arg_p, const jerry_length_t js_arg_cnt, const jerryx_arg_t *c_arg_p, jerry_length_t c_arg_cnt);
functions.description: Transforms the provided JavaScript this value and positional arguments into native C values according to a sequence of jerryx_arg_t transformation steps. c_arg_p must point to an array of at least c_arg_cnt jerryx_arg_t descriptors.

this_val and all entries in js_arg_p must be valid jerry_value_t values created/owned per JerryScript API rules.
The exact mapping/order of c_arg_p steps to this/arguments is not specified in this header (details unknown).

functions.name: jerryx_arg_transform_args
functions.signature: jerry_value_t jerryx_arg_transform_args (const jerry_value_t *js_arg_p, const jerry_length_t js_arg_cnt, const jerryx_arg_t *c_arg_p, jerry_length_t c_arg_cnt);
functions.description: Transforms positional JavaScript arguments into native C values per the provided jerryx_arg_t steps. Use when only arguments (not `this`) need conversion.

import random
from typing import List

# Target: Provide initial interesting buffers for FUZZ_PARAM_STR / FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME.
# Stub uses: FUZZ_PARAM_STR() to supply a C-string for "%s" in format "%s %d" and an int value for %d
# The int comes from FUZZ_PARAM(unsigned int), which is not sourced from our buffer directly in this harness,
# but engines often read multiple chunks from the same input stream. We'll still focus on producing a rich string.
# Requirements for string: valid UTF-8/ASCII, include edge cases: empty, long, whitespace, newlines, percent signs,
# wide unicode, null bytes avoided (C-strings stop at NUL), and embedded formatting tokens to ensure they are treated
# as data (the format string is fixed "%s %d" so any % in the string should be printed literally by %s).

MAX_SIZE = 4096

EDGE_STRINGS: List[str] = [
    "",  # empty
    "hello",  # simple
    " ",  # single space
    "\t\n\r\v\f",  # whitespace set
    "%",  # lone percent (should be safe as argument to %s)
    "100% done",  # percent within text
    "%s %d %x %% literal",  # looks like format tokens but treated as data via %s
    "null\0byte",  # contains NUL: but when passed as C string, it will truncate at first NUL,
                    # to avoid truncation, we will normally not include NUL in final selection unless chosen deliberately
    "🚀✨ unicode rocket and stars",
    "中文测试 — mixed UTF-8",
    "a" * 1024,  # long but reasonable
    "A" * 3000,  # near upper range but leaves room for safety
    "line1\nline2\nline3",
    "path/like/string.ext",
    ",.;:!@#$^&*()[]{}<>?/~`|\\'\"",
]

# We will generally avoid embedded NUL to not truncate; keep an option to include it rarely for variety.

def _rand_unicode_str(rng: random.Random, target_len: int) -> str:
    # Generate a UTF-8 string of approximate length with a mix of categories.
    # Use safe code points commonly supported.
    blocks = [
        (0x20, 0x7E),      # ASCII printable
        (0x00A1, 0x00FF),  # Latin-1 supplement
        (0x0370, 0x03FF),  # Greek
        (0x0400, 0x04FF),  # Cyrillic
        (0x4E00, 0x9FFF),  # CJK Unified Ideographs
        (0x1F300, 0x1F64F) # Emojis and symbols
    ]
    chars = []
    while len(chars) < target_len:
        lo, hi = rng.choice(blocks)
        cp = rng.randint(lo, hi)
        try:
            ch = chr(cp)
            # Exclude surrogate code points
            if 0xD800 <= cp <= 0xDFFF:
                continue
            chars.append(ch)
        except ValueError:
            continue
    return ''.join(chars)


def _build_payload(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Choose base string from curated or random
    choice = rng.random()
    if choice < 0.5:
        s = rng.choice(EDGE_STRINGS)
        # Avoid NUL by default; only include if explicitly selected and with low probability
        if "\0" in s and rng.random() > 0.1:
            s = s.replace("\0", " ")
    else:
        # Construct composite string with varied segments
        parts = []
        # Optional prefix with percents to ensure handling as literal in %s
        if rng.random() < 0.6:
            parts.append(rng.choice(["%", "%%", "100%", "%s-literal%", "%d%% complete"]))
        # Add random words
        word_pool = [
            "JerryScript", "log", "DEBUG", "TRACE", "WARNING", "ERROR",
            "🔥", "测试", "данные", "データ", "데이터", "datos",
            "newline->\n<-here", "tab->\t<-here"
        ]
        for _ in range(rng.randint(2, 6)):
            parts.append(rng.choice(word_pool))
        # Optional long filler
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            parts.append("-" * rng.randint(10, 200))
        # Optional unicode bulk
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            parts.append(_rand_unicode_str(rng, rng.randint(5, 60)))
        s = ' '.join(parts)

    # With small probability, generate a very long string but cap to MAX_SIZE-1
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        tail = _rand_unicode_str(rng, rng.randint(256, 2048))
        s = (s + " " + tail)[:MAX_SIZE - 1]

    # Ensure no embedded NUL unless explicitly decided
    if "\0" in s and rng.random() > 0.05:
        s = s.replace("\0", " ")

    # Encode as UTF-8. FUZZ_PARAM_STR typically reads raw bytes; we'll provide bytes.
    b = s.encode('utf-8', errors='strict')
    # Ensure size cap
    if len(b) > MAX_SIZE:
        b = b[:MAX_SIZE]
    return b


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    return _build_payload(rng)

import random
import os
import struct

# We generate an "arbitrary bytes" buffer that is useful across many JerryScript
# fuzzer stubs which primarily consume FUZZ_PARAM_STR() and FUZZ_PARAM_FILENAME().
# Goals:
# - Provide valid UTF-8/CESU-8 compatible text for string-related APIs.
# - Include JSON snippets for jerry_json_parse.
# - Include RegExp patterns and flags-like sequences for jerry_regexp* paths.
# - Include module specifiers and simple module code fragments (for resolve and parse helpers).
# - Include path-like strings suitable for jerry_port_path_* and filename consumers.
# - Keep size <= 4096 bytes.
# - Make data seeded-random to diversify while remaining valid/interesting.

SAFE_ASCII = (
    [chr(c) for c in range(0x20, 0x7f) if chr(c) not in {'\\', '"'}]
)

WHITESPACE = [" ", "\t", "\n"]

JSON_VALUES = [
    'null', 'true', 'false', '0', '1', '-1', '3.14159', '"str"',
    '[]', '{}', '{"a":1}', '{"nested":{"x":[1,2,3],"y":"z"}}',
]

REGEXP_FRAGMENTS = [
    r"[a-z]+", r"(foo|bar)?", r"^hello$", r"\\d{1,3}", r"[\u00A0-\u00FF]",
    r"a.*?b", r"(?:x|y){2,4}", r"^$", r"[\s\S]", r"^.{0,10}$",
]

WORDS = [
    "alpha", "beta", "gamma", "delta", "epsilon", "zeta", "eta", "theta",
    "iota", "kappa", "lambda", "mu", "nu", "xi", "omicron", "pi", "rho",
    "sigma", "tau", "upsilon", "phi", "chi", "psi", "omega",
]

# A few small JS module bodies and specifiers to help module-related paths
MODULE_SOURCES = [
    "export const y=2;",
    "export default 42;",
    "export function f(x){return x+1}\nexport const v='ok';",
]
MODULE_SPECIFIERS = [
    "./mod.js", "../up.mjs", "/abs/path/mod.mjs", "pkg/name", "file:///tmp/mod.js",
]

# Some path-like strings for port path normalization/base
PATH_FRAGMENTS = [
    "/", ".", "..", "tmp", "var", "usr", "home", "user", "docs", "scripts",
    "libs", "src", "build", "dist", "data", "测试",  # include some utf-8
]


def _rand_unicode_word(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Mix ASCII and some extended UTF-8 to exercise encodings
    base = r.choice(WORDS)
    # Occasionally append some non-ascii
    extras = [
        "ä", "ö", "ü", "ß", "ñ", "ø", "å", "é", "€", "©", "™",
        "日本", "한글", "🙂"
    ]
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        base += r.choice(extras)
    return base


def _make_json(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Create a small valid JSON document
    choice = r.random()
    if choice < 0.3:
        return r.choice(JSON_VALUES)
    elif choice < 0.6:
        # object with a few fields
        kvs = []
        for _ in range(r.randint(1, 4)):
            key = _rand_unicode_word(r)
            val = r.choice(JSON_VALUES)
            kvs.append(f'"{key}": {val}')
        return "{" + ", ".join(kvs) + "}"
    else:
        # array mix
        arr = []
        for _ in range(r.randint(1, 6)):
            arr.append(r.choice(JSON_VALUES))
        return "[" + ", ".join(arr) + "]"


def _make_regexp_pattern(r: random.Random) -> str:
    parts = []
    for _ in range(r.randint(1, 3)):
        parts.append(r.choice(REGEXP_FRAGMENTS))
    return "".join(parts)


def _make_flags_like(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # jerry_regexp flags are independent, but stubs construct from ints; here we supply textual hints
    flags = []
    if r.random() < 0.5: flags.append("g")
    if r.random() < 0.5: flags.append("i")
    if r.random() < 0.5: flags.append("m")
    if r.random() < 0.25: flags.append("y")
    if r.random() < 0.25: flags.append("u")
    if r.random() < 0.25: flags.append("s")
    return "".join(flags)


def _make_path(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Compose a path with components, include separators and possibly UTF-8
    parts = []
    depth = r.randint(1, 5)
    absolute = r.random() < 0.6
    if absolute:
        parts.append("")  # leading slash when joined
    for _ in range(depth):
        parts.append(r.choice(PATH_FRAGMENTS))
    path = "/".join(parts)
    # Occasionally add an extension
    if r.random() < 0.7:
        ext = r.choice([".js", ".mjs", ".json", ".txt", ".snap"])
        if not path.endswith("/"):
            path += ext
    return path or "/"


def _make_module_spec(r: random.Random) -> str:
    if r.random() < 0.5:
        return r.choice(MODULE_SPECIFIERS)
    # or a path-like spec
    return _make_path(r)


def _make_cesu8_like(r: random.Random, s: str) -> bytes:
    # While CESU-8 differs for surrogate pairs, most UTF-8 is acceptable for both.
    # We'll return valid UTF-8 bytes; engine treats as CESU-8 fine for BMP code points.
    return s.encode('utf-8', errors='strict')


def _section(title: str) -> str:
    return f"\n/* {title} */\n"


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Construct a multi-purpose buffer with clearly separated sections so consumers taking
    # arbitrary slices still likely see valid tokens.
    chunks: list[bytes] = []

    # 1) Plain text with mixed words and unicode - good for general strings, size/length, iterate
    text_words = [
        _rand_unicode_word(r) for _ in range(r.randint(5, 15))
    ]
    paragraph = " ".join(text_words)
    chunks.append(_section("TEXT").encode('utf-8'))
    chunks.append(_make_cesu8_like(r, paragraph + "\n"))

    # 2) JSON documents (valid) for jerry_json_parse
    chunks.append(_section("JSON").encode('utf-8'))
    for _ in range(r.randint(1, 3)):
        j = _make_json(r)
        chunks.append(_make_cesu8_like(r, j + "\n"))

    # 3) RegExp patterns and text flags
    chunks.append(_section("REGEXP").encode('utf-8'))
    for _ in range(r.randint(1, 3)):
        pat = _make_regexp_pattern(r)
        flags = _make_flags_like(r)
        line = f"/{pat}/{flags}\n"
        chunks.append(_make_cesu8_like(r, line))

    # 4) Module specifiers and simple module source bodies
    chunks.append(_section("MODULE").encode('utf-8'))
    for _ in range(r.randint(1, 3)):
        spec = _make_module_spec(r)
        body = r.choice(MODULE_SOURCES)
        chunks.append(_make_cesu8_like(r, f"// spec: {spec}\n{body}\n"))

    # 5) Paths for jerry_port_path_* and filenames
    chunks.append(_section("PATHS").encode('utf-8'))
    for _ in range(r.randint(2, 6)):
        p = _make_path(r)
        chunks.append(_make_cesu8_like(r, p + "\n"))

    # 6) Magic strings candidates: short, distinct tokens
    chunks.append(_section("MAGIC").encode('utf-8'))
    for _ in range(r.randint(3, 6)):
        w = r.choice(WORDS)
        chunks.append(_make_cesu8_like(r, w + "\n"))

    # 7) Include some numeric lines for %d logging placeholders and numeric conversions
    chunks.append(_section("NUMBERS").encode('utf-8'))
    nums = [str(r.randint(-10_000, 10_000)) for _ in range(r.randint(5, 12))]
    chunks.append(_make_cesu8_like(r, " ".join(nums) + "\n"))

    # 8) Include some longer lines to test string_to_buffer and size queries
    chunks.append(_section("LONG").encode('utf-8'))
    long_line = " ".join(_rand_unicode_word(r) for _ in range(100))
    chunks.append(_make_cesu8_like(r, long_line + "\n"))

    # 9) A tiny valid snapshot-like header placeholder (not a real snapshot, but harmless text)
    # Avoid generating binary garbage; keep textual to remain valid strings.
    chunks.append(_section("MISC").encode('utf-8'))
    chunks.append(_make_cesu8_like(r, "config=serial:/dev/ttyS0,115200\n"))

    # Concatenate and cap to 4096 bytes
    data = b"".join(chunks)
    if len(data) > 4096:
        data = data[:4096]

    return data
